verses.text: Hiram king of Tyre had always been a friend of David. When he heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father's place, he sent his officials to Solomon.
Solomon sent this message back to Hiram:
"You know that my father David could not build a temple for the name of the LORD his God. He was always fighting wars with the enemies all around him, until the LORD put them under his feet.
But now the LORD my God has given me peace on every side. There are no enemies and no disasters.
So I plan to build a temple for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the temple for my name.'

So now give orders for cedar trees from Lebanon to be cut down for me. My workers will work with your workers, and I will pay your workers whatever wages you decide. You know that none of us can cut timber as well as the people of Sidon."
When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was very happy. He said, "Praise the LORD today! He has given David a wise son to rule over this great nation."
Hiram sent this answer to Solomon: "I have received the message you sent me. I will do everything you want about the cedar logs and the cypress logs.

My workers will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea. I will tie them together into rafts and float them by sea to the place you choose. There I will have them taken apart, and you can collect them. In return, you will do what I want by providing food for my household."
So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar and cypress logs he wanted.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat as food for his household, and twenty measures of pure olive oil. Solomon did this for Hiram year after year.
The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
King Solomon forced men from all over Israel to work for him. There were thirty thousand workers.
He sent them to Lebanon in groups of ten thousand men each month. They spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labour.
Solomon also had seventy thousand men who carried loads and eighty thousand men who cut stone in the hills.
Besides these, there were three thousand three hundred foremen in charge of the work, who directed the workers.
At the king's command, they cut large, expensive blocks of stone to make a foundation of shaped stones for the temple.
Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and men from Gebal cut and prepared the timber and the stone for building the temple.
